operational_learning.text: Build the AAR from a Python data file per batch and verify every proposal's old text (exactly once, at the declared line) in the same script that writes the JSON; it removes hand-escaping errors and stale line numbers

The deployed /delegate (v2.4, ~/.claude/skills/delegate/SKILL.md) names the signal PERMISSION_DENIED; the repo working copy (shared/skills/delegate/SKILL.md line 298) and RFC 0011 use WRITE_BLOCKED, one case of the deployment lag of RFC 3.9.2. A delegate that loads the deployed skill meets the older name, so the delegation prompt must state the signal it wants

Three checks run on an RFC cost little and find reference defects that reading misses: refcheck.pl (every clause number, settled point and numbering gap), appxcheck.pl (the 'Carried in' column of appendix A against the decision ids cited in the body) and apply_sim.py (apply every proposal to a copy and re-run the checks); they are in the scratch directory of this mission and are candidates for harvesting as check-rfc scripts

The scanner's hits are about one third true defects: possessives ('s), code spans and quoted prose dominate; its abbreviation, informal and lower-2119 checks were the useful ones, and a capital-token census (caps.pl) found the unexpanded abbreviations (CLI, SITREP, SPOTREP) that the scanner's list missed
